lesson.opening: Why did disputes over doctrine reorganize political authority and everyday institutions?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Doctrine and ecclesiastical jurisdiction

Printing, rulers, and religious communities

Religious settlement and continuing conflict

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Treat religious convictions as historical causes while also examining jurisdiction, dynastic interests, and institutional resources. Neither “only religion” nor “only politics” is sufficient.

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “Luther’s indulgence controversy” or “Peace of Westphalia”?

activities.prompt: “The Reformation happened only because rulers wanted church property.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: This is a reduction to one motive. Test it against doctrine, personal commitment, political settings, and chronology.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
Separate a theological disagreement from a dispute over who has the right to rule or judge.
